limitations: PROGENy and CytoSig signatures are both inferred from bulk gene-expression profiles; a high Spearman correlation between two inferred signatures reflects shared transcriptional drivers or co-regulated gene sets, not causal pathway activation. Correlation does not establish that one pathway drives the other.

All 602 eligible pairs share the same 1,206 cell lines (n = 1,206 for every pair), so the matched-cell-line count does not differentiate pairs; ranking is driven entirely by the correlation magnitude.
The OLS fit is descriptive: the slope of 4.16 reflects the ratio of z-score scales between the two signature families and should not be interpreted as a biological effect size.
The 12 largest-residual cell lines include non-cancerous lines (e.g., NHAHTDD, PrEC LH) whose biology may differ fundamentally from cancer lines, potentially inflating residuals.

The significance label supplied in the source data was not used for filtering, per the study protocol; some pairs may have p-values that would not survive multiple-testing correction across 602 comparisons.

limitations: Correlated inferred signatures (PROGENy, CytoSig) are computational estimates of pathway activity from bulk gene expression; they do not measure direct pathway activation and their correlation does not prove causal pathway relationships.
Z-scores are computed within the cell-line cohort, so they reflect relative expression across cell lines rather than absolute pathway activity in any biological context.
The OLS fit assumes a linear relationship; the large residuals in the top-12 table indicate that non-linear or context-dependent effects may exist for extreme cell lines.
The analysis uses all cell lines measured by both platforms (n = 1,206) without stratification by tissue of origin, so tissue-specific biology is not isolated.

limitations: Both PROGENy and CytoSig scores are inferred from the same underlying gene-expression measurements; high inter-signature correlation is partly mechanical (shared input genes) and cannot be interpreted as independent biological validation.
The OLS fit uses all 1,206 cell lines without stratification by tissue of origin; the slope and R² may be driven by between-tissue variance rather than within-tissue pathway regulation.

The 'significant' label supplied by HPA was not used as a filter, per the study design; some cell lines carry a 'Non-significant' flag (e.g., KYSE-520 for TGFB1) and are included in the correlation and OLS calculations.

The correlation matrix covers 14 PROGENy × 43 CytoSig signatures; signatures with fewer than 30 shared finite-z-score cell lines would be excluded, but all 602 pairs met the threshold in this dataset.
